slicingRule: Each issue must deliver observable player value across UI, orchestration, deterministic domain logic, persistence, tests, and mobile acceptance where applicable.

issues.title: Start and complete a persistent mobile trade
issues.userValue: A player can start Ocean Trader on a phone, accept one contract, complete one voyage with one event, receive settlement, and return later to the persisted campaign.
scope: new campaign with one viable vessel
small port/cargo seed catalog sufficient for first route
deterministic voyage progression and seeded event
financial transaction ledger and one-time settlement
acceptance: At 390x844, player completes new campaign -> contract -> voyage -> event -> settlement without desktop-only interaction.
Reload restores cash, vessel location/state, campaign time, and completed contract state.
Identical state + seed + commands produces identical domain output.
Contract cannot settle twice.
Automated unit/integration tests cover deterministic voyage, settlement, and save schema.

issues.title: Manage an active fleet from the phone
issues.userValue: A player can understand several simultaneous voyages, see what needs attention, inspect a vessel, and advance time from a mobile fleet surface.
scope: five simultaneous active vessels in test scenario
vessel detail with route, ETA, fuel, condition, cargo
acceptance: Five active voyages remain understandable at phone portrait width without horizontal table scrolling.
Attention items are distinguishable from normal voyages without relying on color alone.
All voyages progress independently and restore correctly after reload.

issues.title: Navigate the global fleet on a touch world map
issues.userValue: A player can use the phone map to find ports and vessels, inspect a route and ETA, and move between map and fleet context without losing place.
scope: 20+ real ports with licensed factual coordinates
vessel and port hit testing with enlarged touch targets
acceptance: Touch-only user can select vessel and port, pan, zoom, inspect ETA, and return to prior map state.
Five simultaneous routes are distinguishable on supported phone viewport.
Low zoom does not render all labels persistently.

issues.title: Dock a vessel with touch controls
issues.userValue: A player can perform a skill-based harbour arrival on a phone and see the operational consequence return to the campaign.
acceptance: Normal docking is achievable with touch only on supported smartphone.
Fast collision and grounding produce distinct bounded consequences.
Rotating viewport does not reset active manoeuvre.
No browser scrolling interferes with active manoeuvre controls.
Harbour result is persisted exactly once in campaign state.

issues.title: Buy, sell, refuel, and maintain ships
issues.userValue: A player can turn voyage profit into fleet decisions and manage vessel readiness rather than only repeating contracts.
scope: at least four materially different ship classes
acceptance: Player can compare ship alternatives on phone without desktop table dependency.
Buying/selling and repair/refuel transactions are attributable in ledger.
Condition materially affects at least cost, reliability, resale, or performance.

issues.title: Finance fleet growth and understand leverage
issues.userValue: A player can finance a vessel, understand repayment risk before committing, and see debt affect company value and future choices.
scope: principal, financing cost, schedule, and default consequence
insolvency warning for directly calculable dangerous actions
acceptance: Player can explain total immediate and scheduled commitment from the confirmation screen.
Debt and repayments survive save/load.
Company value includes liabilities correctly.
A financing transaction cannot be applied twice.

issues.title: Make route and market choices matter
issues.userValue: A player sees different cargo/port opportunities and must trade margin, deadline, fuel, condition, repositioning, and risk instead of following one dominant route.
acceptance: At least three test scenarios prefer different choices under different fleet/market states.
No single seeded route/cargo dominates the defined balance scenarios.
Expected major costs and risk remain visible before commitment.

issues.title: Progress the company through shipping eras
issues.userValue: A successful campaign changes over time through new vessel technology, operating constraints, and opportunities rather than remaining a static endless loop.
acceptance: Advancing between defined eras changes at least one strategic fleet or market decision.
Old saves migrate safely across era-data version changes.
Era progression remains understandable on mobile without encyclopedic prerequisite knowledge.
